member.name: M:SimioAPI.ICalendar.ScheduleCurrentEvent(System.Object,SimioAPI.CalendarEventHandler)
member.summary: Called to schedule an event on the calendar to run as soon as possible. This call is thread safe. It can be called from any thread, and is the recommended way to "marshal" code from some "event" thread to the main run thread. Callbacks scheduled this way are not guaranteed to run immediately, but will run as a soon as the main Simio calendar loop runs them, which for many purposes will be the "current" simulation time.
member.remarks: Note that internally this method simply inserts the callback into an unbounded concurrent queue, which the run thread then dequeues from at the beginning of the standard event loop. Thus, many calls to this method at once have the ability to "stall" the run thread as it dequeues callbacks that have just been queued on another thread. If it is found that events from the event source are occuring with little time between them, using standard debounce/throttling techniques (such as recording the last time a call was made and only make another after some given time span) should help alleviate a "flood" of callbacks being put on the queue. Calling this method when the simulation is not actually running (for example paused or stopped), will result in a returned with the value false. This occurs because scheduling an event while the simulation is not running will simply aggregate the callbacks in the callback queue, which results in either an unbounded growing memory cost, or a long wait the next time the simulation starts (for example, coming out of a pause), while that queue is drained.

member.name: P:SimioAPI.ISimioProject.SupportSourceControl
member.summary:
This setting affects how Simio writes its project files. The default value is False and is appropriate for most cases where a single user edits the project file. Simio will digitally sign the file, which is necessary to allow certain lower editions of Simio to open files created by other editions. Simio will also include other optional information in the file, such as window layouts, view settings, and the project's save history. It will also create backup files when saving.
In some cases, however, multiple users can work on the same Simio project, typically by saving the project file using Simio's .simproj format and storing it in a version control system. Setting Support Source Control to True can help avoid conflicts when users merge their changes. In this case, Simio will not sign files and will exclude certain other information from the project file. When the project is ready to be distributed, Support Source Control can be set to False, and the project saved again (usually to a new name or location, using Simio's.spfx file format), thereby enabling normal project behavior.
